title: Orndorff's four goals lead Frankfort boys in 9-1 playoff rout of Philip Barbour | Mineral County WV News and Tribune | wvnews.com
text:
SHORT GAP, W.Va. (WV News) – Liam Orndorff turned in a four-goal performance, Noah Weaver tallied two goals, and Cohen Hartman, Jesus Perdew, and Wyatt Kesner each scored one goal as Frankfort defeated Philip Barbour, 9-1, in playoff action on Wednesday. Phili Barbour’s lone goal was scored by Matthew Whitehair.
With the win, Frankfort advances to host Petersburg in next-round action on Saturday, Oct. 25 at 5 p.m.
Frankfort, the No. 1 seed, entered the contest after posting a regular season record of 11-4-3.
Philip Barbour, the No. 8 seed, entered the contest after posting a regular season record of 1-15-1, and after defeating Lincoln, the No. 9 seed.
“It was a good performance. I was happy that we didn’t take a lot of time to get into the goal scoring. I think within the first 12 minutes, we had four goals, and that’s what we wanted. We talked about that, that we needed to get out of this goal-scoring slump. And honestly, we worked on that all week, producing and creating goals, and that’s exactly what we did, Frankfort coach Jason Vaughan stated.
According to Vaughan, “The concern coming into this game is that if you don’t put a good performance together, the boys would start questioning themselves. And that’s not going to happen now, they’re going to go into that game on Saturday confident and ready to come out and get another one. So, I’m just really happy with the performance we put up, and I think this will be a real momentum builder.”
“The most important thing as you continue to advance is to do it with a healthy, rested group of guys. We were able to do that tonight. Everyone got to play, it was great for morale, but it’s also good for some boys to get a little bit of a rest, because this is a stretch of really important games. So, if we can rest them and keep them in great shape for the upcoming games that’s great,” Vaughan explained.
Frankfort shot out to a 5-0 lead at the half, then outscored Philip Barbour 4-1 in the second half in earning the 9-1 victory.
The Falcons’ Liam Orndorff got Frankfort on the board first with a penalty kick goal at the 36:06 mark, just shy of four minutes into the game. Orndorff added another at the 33:00 mark to put the Falcons up 2-0.
Noah Weaver scored the next goal for Frankfort (31:47), then Orndorff added two more goals (28:08 and 14:34) to put the Falcons up 5-0 at the half.
After the break, Cohen Hartman scored for Frankfort on a header (34:25), then Weaver scored another goal (32:40) to extend the Falcons’ lead to 7-0.
Philip Barbour finally got on the board on a penalty kick goal from Matthew Whitehair with 22:30 remaining in the game.
Jesus Perdew delivered a long-distance shot (18:35) and Wyatt Kesner put in a goal (6:18) to bring Frankfort’s winning tally to 9-1.
With the loss, Philip Barbour’s season concludes with an overall record of 2-16-1.
“We only have three seniors. We’re a very young team. We play Frankfort next year in the very beginning, and we’re looking forward to it, because our freshmen now will have more experience and they’ll be ready to play,” Philip Barbour assistant coach Chris Anglin stated.
According to Anglin, “As for tonight, despite the result, they didn’t give up, and that’s all I could ask out of them.”
